plugins.name: code-comments
plugins.description: Comment discipline for any language — what earns a comment and what gets deleted. Sweeps comment noise out of changed code before a commit or while fixing PR feedback.

plugins.name: humanizer
plugins.description: Edit outbound prose so it reads human-written, not AI-generated — PR replies, commit messages, Jira/Confluence comments, emails, docs. Based on Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing" guide.

plugins.name: amag-pr-respond
plugins.description: Address review feedback on your own work — reviewer comments on a Bitbucket PR you authored, or the findings a local amag-pr-review saved for a ticket worktree. Investigates, fixes, replies, and teaches amag-pr-review what it missed. AMAG-specific.

plugins.name: ticket-quest
plugins.description: Take assigned Jira tickets from investigation through to a verified implementation — an isolated git worktree per ticket, a Sonnet orchestrator that routes bounded work by cost (Haiku scout, Sonnet engineer, Opus for hard or security-sensitive changes), consults a Fable advisor only on escalation, and verifies every delegated claim.

plugins.name: design-tournament
plugins.description: Run competing code designs through blind judging — three stance-diverse designers, three fresh judges scoring against a rubric fixed beforehand, then a synthesis that grafts the best ideas from the designs that lost.

plugins.name: amag-raise-bug
plugins.description: Raise bug and task tickets in AMAG's Symmetry Jira — duplicate check, every claim verified against the code, the team's field layout, and drafts shown before anything is created. AMAG-specific.

plugins.name: amag-pr-review
plugins.description: Review a Bitbucket pull request or a ticket worktree under C:\repos\ticket-work with Sonnet reviewers per dimension (Opus at high), an Opus verify pass, and incremental re-review. Built for AMAG's Symmetry and Sentinel repos. AMAG-specific.

plugins.name: visual-inspection
plugins.description: Inspect screenshots and local screen recordings on a small token budget — compare before/after UI screenshots, crop and zoom the changed regions, sample video frames, and find scene changes or static stretches, all prepared locally with ImageMagick and FFmpeg.

plugins.name: grilling
plugins.description: Stress-test a plan, decision or idea by being interviewed about it — questions asked in rounds over a tree of decisions, each with a recommended answer. From Matt Pocock's skills.

plugins.name: domain-modeling
plugins.description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model while you design — challenge fuzzy or conflicting terms, keep GLOSSARY.md current as terms are settled, and record ADRs for hard-to-reverse decisions. From Matt Pocock's skills.

plugins.name: grill-with-docs
plugins.description: Run grilling and domain-modeling together with one command, so the interview about a plan also writes the glossary and ADRs as you go. Needs both plugins. From Matt Pocock's skills.

plugins.name: change-diagrams
plugins.description: Diagram a code change — a bug fix, a feature or a refactor — as one Artifact page: before/after sequence figures with lanes, numbered steps and a Why column, flow figures and a rig-results table, all from one house template that works in light and dark.
